reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a tutorial-style online earning demonstration focused on learning a system rather than documenting victimization or proven deception. The blockchain-account condition, BTC wallet instructions, mining-plan language, and BTC-denominated balances are described as instructional or promotional elements, with no indication that credentials were misused, funds were taken, payouts failed, or the creator knowingly solicited a deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: New site: $ 5 a month without any kind of investment! Watch this video to know the system!
take the address of BTC wallet from your crypto account so I am clicking here and taking request then see currency, select your bitcoin then you will copy the address from here

opening.argument: The offer connects unusually easy earnings to concrete viewer actions. The description promises "$5 a month" without investment and tells viewers to watch to learn the system, while the title presents earning money without investment as the central proposition. The video also presents a completed order and roughly $200 allegedly obtained without investment, making the claimed reward part of the participation pitch rather than a general discussion. On screen, registration is tied to free spins, an earning balance, and a withdrawal button. Together, these are the structure of a low-barrier reward funnel: watch, register or follow the demonstrated process, and expect a cryptocurrency-linked payout.

citations.quote: New site: $ 5 a month without any kind of investment! Watch this video to know the system!
here is the payment i have received and I have payed interest so if you want to count the usds here is 20.96 usds so here I got around 200 USD without any investment

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a tutorial does not neutralize the solicitation. The description does not merely explain a concept: it advertises a specific monthly return and directs viewers to learn the system. The speaker likewise presents a completed order and claimed payment, which supplies the testimonial-like incentive the defense overlooks. No proof of a failed payout is required to identify a reward claim tied to participation; the relevant concern is that the promised benefit is used to induce the viewer to follow the process.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These materials show an advertised earning opportunity and a demonstration, but they do not show that a viewer was deceived or that the displayed reward could not be obtained. The $5 statement is promotional wording, while the speaker's claimed payment and completed request are presented as evidence of the workflow, not proof of a fraudulent transaction. The dashboard's balance and withdrawal control likewise show interface elements, not a confirmed successful withdrawal or victim loss.

citations.quote: Watch this video to know the system!
here is the payment i have received

opening.argument: The strongest risk signal is the combination of recurring mining returns with a paid plan. The displayed starter offer requires 0.015 BTC, describes a 365-day contract, promises 3.333% per day and 0.0005 BTC per day, and presents a Buy Now control. Elsewhere, the page calls itself a source of real-time payouts and tells users to select a Bitcoin mining plan to start earning. These are not merely abstract cryptocurrency references: a package purchase is placed next to a specific, recurring mining-income promise. The unusually high daily percentage, long contract, and immediate purchase pathway make the promotion materially deceptive in presentation even without an independently verified loss.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the absence of documented victimization as dispositive, but the visible offer itself is the relevant evidence. A 365-day contract, a Buy Now button, and a stated daily percentage establish the purchase-to-recurring-income linkage. The defense also concedes that the material is promotional. That framing makes the return figures more consequential, not less: viewers are being shown a concrete mining plan and payout presentation without any substantiated basis for the advertised rate.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The frames establish that a mining-plan interface displays terms, but they do not establish that the plan was fraudulent, that the advertised percentage was impossible, or that anyone purchased it and lost money. A Buy Now button shows an available action, not a completed transaction. The reference evidence therefore supports classifying the content as an operational demonstration while leaving the site's safety and returns unverified.

opening.argument: Although the speaker uses an instructional format, the content functions as promotion for an investment-style earning system. The page explicitly labels the offer "Our Investment Plans" and tells viewers they can increase daily passive income by selecting a plan and generating revenue. A displayed starter plan couples a BTC amount and a 365-day contract with a daily percentage and daily BTC return. The speaker then demonstrates wallet-address handling and requests, giving the audience an operational route into the offer. This is not neutral education about blockchain: the tutorial format is the mechanism that makes the passive-return solicitation actionable.

citations.quote: take the address of BTC wallet from your crypto account so I am clicking here and taking request then see currency, select your bitcoin then you will copy the address from here

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's description of an operational demonstration actually confirms the promotional function. The content does not stop at explaining blockchain concepts; it walks viewers through the wallet step while the site displays investment plans and passive income. The absence of proven misuse does not turn a return-driven participation pitch into neutral education. The relevant question is what the presentation steers viewers toward, and the answer is selecting a plan and pursuing recurring income.

citations.quote: you will copy the address from here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Instructional guidance and promotional context can coexist without proving a scam. The wallet-address excerpt shows how the presenter performs a request, but it does not show that viewers were required to surrender credentials, that funds were taken, or that the plan failed. The investment-plan screen demonstrates what the site displays; it does not independently verify or disprove its returns. Thus the argument establishes promotion, not deception.
